slides.headline: October 16, 2014: India launched the third satellite of a navigation system it was building entirely on its own.
ISRO launched IRNSS-1C aboard a PSLV-C26 rocket from Sriharikota
slides.body: The 1,425 kg satellite was the third of seven planned for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System - what would later be called NavIC - reaching its intended orbit about 20 minutes after liftoff.

slides.headline: It was ISRO's 28th PSLV flight, and the seventh in the rocket's most powerful XL configuration.
slides.body: The President of India issued a formal note of congratulations, calling it a step toward India having its own satellite-based navigation system - independent of the GPS systems built and controlled by other countries.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs navigation infrastructure it doesn't have to borrow from anyone else.
slides.body: Building a satellite constellation one launch at a time, rather than relying on a foreign system, gave India a navigation capability under its own control - for its military, its ships, and eventually its phones.
